rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for reacting wildly or irrationally under stress.

example.english: I freak out whenever I hear that the report has gone wrong.
example.traditional: 我一聽到份報告出錯就發癲喇。
example.jyutping: ngo5 jat1 teng1 dou3 fan6 bou3 gou3 ceot1 co3 zau6 faat3 din1 laa3

rows.note: Use this when the emphasis is on losing control of one's behaviour rather than simply becoming frightened or upset.

example.english: They completely freak out as soon as they get on stage and start shouting.
example.traditional: 佢哋一上台就完全失控，仲大嗌添。
example.jyutping: keoi5 dei6 jat1 soeng5 toi1 zau6 jyun4 cyun4 sat1 hung3 zung6 daai6 aai3 tim1

rows.note: Use this specifically when someone freaks out in a panicky, flustered way and cannot think or act properly.

example.english: I freak whenever I have to go on stage at short notice and cannot even hold my script properly.
example.traditional: 我一聽到要即刻上台就會慌晒手腳，連份稿都拎唔穩。
example.jyutping: ngo5 jat1 teng1 dou3 jiu3 zik1 hak1 soeng5 toi4 zau6 wui5 fong1 saai3 sau2 goek3 lin4 fan6 gou2 dou1 ling1 m4 wan2
